properties.address: The Old Post Office, 58 Upper Harlestone, Northampton, Northamptonshire NN7 4EH
properties.description: This delightful period stone house stands in an enviable position adjacent to and backing onto open pasture forming part of the Althorp Estate in one of the most sought after locations in Northamptonshire. The house is believed to date from the early 19th Century constructed of ironstone beneath a part thatch and part slate roof and offers considerable scope for modernisation and refurbishment to the three bedroomed accommodation with potential for extension into the attached outbuilding subject to planning permission. Formally the village Post Office and now vacant the property retains a wealth of character features and stands in private gardens extending to just under a quarter of an acre. Tenure Freehold The property stands in the Harlestone village Conservation Area and is NOT a Listed building. The house forms part of the Althorp Estate and will be sold subject the Estate standard schedule of covenants. ACCOMMODATION GROUND FLOOR Reception hall, living room, Post Office servery, store, cloakroom, dining room, kitchen, pantry and porch. FIRST FLOOR Landing, bedroom one, bedroom two, bedroom three, bath/shower room. OUTSIDE The house stands back from the road behind the deep front garden bounded by paled fencing and a pathway leads to the front door flanked either side by lawns and well stocked flower and shrub borders containing a variety of mature small trees including Holly, Laurel, Oak, Sumac and Magnolia. The garden continues on the eastern side of the house where there is a former kitchen garden once used for the production of vegetables and bounded by post and rail fencing. A doorway leads to the courtyard. OUTBUILDINGS Workshop, fuel store, wood store and external WC. REAR GARDEN Laid to lawn housing the now derelict greenhouse and the oil storage tank, the rear garden is bounded by post and rail fencing and Beech hedging and contains a number of mature shrubs and small trees backing directly onto open pasture. HISTORICAL NOTE AND PLANNING The property stands in the Harlestone village Conservation Area and is NOT a Listed building. The house forms part of the Althorp Estate and will be sold subject the Estate standard schedule of covenants. AGENTS NOTE THE GARDEN STANDING TO THE EASTERN SIDE OF THE HOUSE WAS ONCE USED FOR THE PRODUCTION OF VEGETABLES AND IS BOUNDED BY POST AND RAIL FENCING. THIS AREA IS EXCLUDED FROM THE SALE BY AUCTION HOWEVER, IT WILL BE OFFERED TO THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER BY SEPARATE CONTRACT AT A PRICE OF £35,000 IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING THE COMPLETION OF THE SALE. SHOULD THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER FAIL TO TAKE UP THE OPTION TO PURCHASE WITHIN FOUR WEEKS, THIS LAND WILL BE RETAINED BY THE ALTHORP ESTATE, AND THE BUYER WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ERECTING NEW BOUNDARY FENCES AND WALLS ALONG THE PARTY BOUNDARY. Energy Efficiency Rating (EPC) Current Rating E Services Interested parties are requested to make their own enquiries to the relevant authorities as to the availability of services. properties.description: Commercial Development Auction House Birmingham are proud to present this former brass foundry and ironmongers, offering investors and developers the opportunity to explore a new future for a distinctive piece of Wolverhampton’s industrial heritage. Historically associated with William Evans, Son & Co., the site’s manufacturing roots extend back to around 1854, with the present building believed to date from around 1870. The company’s activities included brass founding and lock manufacturing, followed by its longstanding role as an ironmongers and builders’ merchant. Council heritage records describe the property as a rare surviving example of a nineteenth-century industrial complex within the City, a compelling story for an investor seeking a project with its own identity. Customer WC facilities are provided, together with a dedicated fire exit. Externally, the premises benefit from an established and attractive outside seating area, incorporating decking and covered seating. The upper parts of the property comprise a self-contained residential flat, accessed independently from Duke Street, and provides entrance hallway with staircase rising to the main accommodation with spacious lounge with front-facing bay window, modern fitted kitchen / dining room, two bedrooms and family bathroom. properties.description: A charming and beautifully preserved Grade II listed four-bedroom cottage, ideally located in the highly sought-after heart of Warwick town centre. This unique and characterful home offers a rare opportunity to acquire not only a stunning period home, but also an accompanying commercial unit with exceptional potential. The property is arranged over two floors and provides generous and versatile living accommodation, comprising four well-proportioned bedrooms, an inviting lounge, a separate dining room, and an updated kitchen. Throughout the home, an abundance of original features can be admired, including exposed wooden beams and historic detailing. The property benefits from a delightful rear courtyard, offering a private and versatile outdoor space ideal for entertaining. Several useful outbuildings are included, two of which benefit from restroom facilities, further enhancing the flexibility of this unique space. archive.address: Horsforth Cemetery Chapel, Calverley Lane, Horsforth, Leeds, West Yorkshire LS18 4DZ
archive.description: A former Victorian cemetery chapel situated within the grounds of Horsforth Cemetery and offering potential for restoration and alternative use. Dating from 1881, the stone-built property is of Gothic Revival design and features a central square tower topped by a tall slated spire. Other architectural details include pitched slate roofs, pointed-arched openings, stone buttresses, carved crosses and a traceried window. Internally, the accommodation includes the principal former chapel and worship space, together with additional rooms arranged over the ground and first floors. The building retains stained-glass windows and a number of period features. The property represents an unique opportunity for a purchaser seeking a character building with potential for a range of alternative uses, subject to obtaining the necessary consents. Prospective purchasers should satisfy themselves regarding the building’s condition, services, internal configuration and suitability for their intended use. The property is situated within the established grounds of Horsforth Cemetery, approximately five miles north-west of Leeds city centre. The cemetery can be accessed from Calverley Lane and Victoria Mount, with the chapel approached via the internal cemetery roads. Horsforth is a popular and well-established suburb offering a range of shops, cafés, restaurants and other amenities, principally around Town Street and New Road Side. The area benefits from good road and public transport connections, including rail services from Horsforth station and access to Leeds city centre, Bradford and Leeds Bradford Airport.

archive.description: **FOR SALE BY LIVE STREAMED ONLINE AUCTION 22ND OCTOBER 2026** The property comprises a vacant, detached C-listed building of up to two storeys, occupying a site of approximately 853 m. Constructed primarily of light-coloured granite, the side and rear walls feature square-hammered rubble, while the front elevation is finished in close-jointed hammer-blocked ashlar. Architectural features include predominantly pointed-arched plate tracery openings, some enhanced with hood mouldings. archive.address: 21A&21B Green Lane, Sale, M33 5PN
archive.description: TO BE SOLD BY AUCTION ON 11-12TH NOVEMBER 2026 UNLESS SOLD PRIOR UNDER AUCTION TERMS. 21A&21B Green Lane, Sale, M33 5PN An attractive mixed commercial investment comprising two modern units on a single title, offering established rental income from 21A alongside a vacant and highly versatile commercial unit at 21B. 21A Green Lane comprises approximately 690 sq ft of retail accommodation with around 200 sq ft of frontage and is currently occupied as a vape shop. The unit is let on a full repairing and insuring (FRI) lease signed in 2026 at £1,550 pcm / £18,600 per annum inclusive of VAT, plus a £450 annual insurance contribution. The lease includes a rent review/increase provision in year three, providing scope for future rental growth in accordance with the lease terms. Accommodation includes a glazed shopfront, electric shutters, kitchen, WC, tiled flooring, LED lighting, fire alarm and single-phase power. 21B Green Lane is accessed independently to the rear of the property and is currently vacant, providing approximately 678 sq ft of workshop and office accommodation, together with a further 250 sq ft secure external area. Previously used as an electrical repair workshop, the unit offers flexible potential for a variety of commercial uses including workshop, technical/laboratory space, offices or other small business occupation, subject to any necessary consents. The unit includes two offices, fitted workbenches and storage, kitchen, WC, secure stockroom, extensive power provision including single- and three-phase power, HVAC and rear bifold gates providing approximately four-metre delivery access. Plant and inventory stated by the vendor to be worth approximately £45,000 are included within the sale. For investors, the vacant 21B unit provides an opportunity to establish a second rental income stream and potentially significantly increase the overall income from the property, with combined rental income potentially approaching £40,000 per annum, subject to the rent achieved on 21B. Alternatively, the unit may appeal to an owner-occupier looking to operate from the rear while retaining the income from 21A. Both units are reported to benefit from A-rated EPCs. The property occupies its own standalone plot and is understood to be of steel-frame construction, offering a versatile building layout with potential for future first-floor extension, subject to structural suitability and all necessary consents. Situated in the centre of Ashton-on-Mersey village, the property is well positioned amongst a range of independent retailers, cafés, restaurants and local amenities, with Sale town centre and Metrolink connections also within easy reach. A strong opportunity combining immediate commercial rental income with a vacant second unit offering further letting, owner-occupation and income-growth potential. Updated photographs and floorplans will be added shortly. Important Information Tenure: Freehold

The property incorporates a range of communal living and dining areas, office accommodation, ancillary storage, staff facilities, five bedrooms with en-suite facilities, additional kitchen and lounge accommodation, together with external yard areas, providing a well-configured operational layout for the tenant. Saint Johns House occupies a prominent position on Prospect Row within Sunderland city centre, benefitting from excellent access to a wide range of retail, leisure and public transport amenities. Sunderland Railway and Metro Station are within walking distance, whilst the nearby A19 and A690 provide excellent regional connectivity throughout the North East. Sunderland continues to benefit from significant regeneration and investment, reinforcing its position as a well-established commercial centre with strong long-term occupational demand.

archive.address: 29 Brislington Hill, Brislington, Bristol, BS4 5BE
archive.description: A Leasehold Commercial Property comprising a retail unit on Brislington Hill, forming part of the busy Concourse shopping parade on the A4 Bath Road in the Brislington area of Bristol. Understood to be offered with vacant possession following the expiry of the previous five year lease in August 2026, the lot will suit investors and owner-occupiers seeking a low-entry shop unit to let or trade from on an established parade. Arranged across ground and first floors, the property was most recently let to a private individual on a five year full repairing and insuring lease from 03/08/2021 at 7,600 per annum, which expired on 02/08/2026. The property benefits from a shop frontage to Brislington Hill with ancillary accommodation to the first floor, and neighbouring units on the parade have recently let at between 7,500 and 9,600 per annum. Lease information - approximately 69 years unexpired (please refer to the legal pack). Please note this property is elected for VAT. Brislington Hill forms part of the mid-1960s Brislington Hill and Concourse shopping parade fronting the A4 Bath Road in Brislington, about two miles south-east of Bristol city centre and roughly two miles from Bristol Temple Meads railway station. The parade benefits from a pedestrian overpass and large residential blocks immediately behind it, with rear access and public parking off Church Hill and Glenarm Road. Brislington Park and Ride on Bath Road, about half a mile to the south-east, runs the First bus service 9 into Temple Meads and the city centre, Tesco Extra at Callington Road is about half a mile away and Brislington Enterprise College on Hungerford Road is the nearest secondary school. The A4 links to the A4174 Ring Road and the A37, with the M32 and M4 reached via the city centre.

archive.description: Town & Country Property Auctions are delighted to offer For Sale by Public Auction this exceptional Commercial and Redevelopment Opportunity: The Old Brewery, Bay Tree Hill, Liskeard. Occupying a prime position in the very heart of Liskeard Town Centre, this substantial historic landmark extends to approximately 13,351 sq ft across four levels and comprises two original townhouses together with a former brewery building. Currently home to a range of established businesses including retail units, a café, offices and storage facilities, the property generates immediate commercial use while offering enormous future development potential. This rare town-centre site presents a compelling opportunity for developers and investors to create a high-density mixed-use scheme. Subject to the necessary consents, the upper floors and brewery sections offer scope for conversion into 10–15 apartments, while the original townhouses could be restored as premium character residences. The extensive lower ground floor and storage areas also provide potential for valuable off-street parking or additional commercial accommodation. Situated on the prominent Bay Tree Hill, the property benefits from excellent visibility, strong local footfall and convenient access to shops, amenities and the mainline railway station. Opportunities of this scale are seldom available. This historic but tired landmark is a true sleeping giant, offering significant asset enhancement and redevelopment uplift in one of Cornwall's most established market towns. archive.address: Leasowe Castle Hotel, Leasowe Road, Wirral, CH46 3RF
archive.description: Online auction 12th-13th October 2026 Grade 2* Listed Hotel with 48 Ensuite Letting Rooms This Grade 2* listed hotel offers 48 en-suite letting rooms along with 4 large function rooms and 30 additional restaurant dining areas. Externally there is also onsite parking for approx. 70 vehicles. The total site area covers approx. 2.24 hectares / 5.53 acres with the internal floor area totalling approx. 4,598.3 m2 / 49,496 sqft. The accommodation of the property comprises of: Conference and Function Accommodation: The hotel has significant conference/banqueting capability with the largest room being the Castle Suite, to the rear and on the ground floor, capable of seating up to 250 diners (circa 300 theatre style) but also able to divide into two smaller rooms of approximately half the size each. This room has the benefit of its own bar servery area and is located immediately adjacent to the main hotel kitchens. There is also a raised stage/performance area to the extreme west side of the room. To the rear this has been converted to a further function room known as ‘The Keep’ and is used for civil ceremonies, capable of seating circa 100+ people. At first floor level is a private meeting/function/dining room capable of seating circa 38 people. Both these elements can be separately accessed directly from the car park area. To the first floor is a further function room known as the Turret Suite, which comprises two interconnecting rooms to the eastern side of the hotel, partially within the 1987 addition and above the Wreckers Bar and coffee shop. These rooms have a seated capacity of circa 100. Reception Area / Lounges: The main reception office/desk and reception hall are located at ground floor level of the original towers on the east facing elevation and accessed directly from the car park. The entrance hall benefits from an attractive feature staircase leading to the letting bedrooms within the upper floors of the turrets. To the immediate right of the ground floor reception hall is the Star Chamber Lounge which has been furnished with various chairs, settees and coffee tables. There is also a 4-passenger lift (300kg) giving access between the ground floor and third floor. Food and Beverage (F&B) Areas: The Wreckers Bar and adjoining coffee shop are situated at ground floor level within the 1987addition. The Wreckers Bar has a seated capacity of circa 30 and has its own separate access as well as the benefit of access to the enclosed side external lawned area which doubles as a beer garden. The Coffee shop has a seated capacity of circa 16 and is situated between the Wreckers Bar and the main reception hall (and can accessed from either). Each contain a bar servery. In addition, accessed via a corridor from the main reception hall, is the Brasserie 1593 restaurant area, which has a dining capacity of circa 30 and which also has its own bar servery area. Letting Bedrooms: The hotel provides a total of 48 letting bedrooms situated at first, second and third floor levels throughout the property. A total of 8 rooms are situated within the original castellated section (2 at first floor level and 6 and second floor level including two suites/four poster bedrooms) and the remaining 40 rooms are provided towards the rear, within the 1900’s section (15 at first, 16 at second and 9 at third floor levels). All rooms are either provided with double or twin beds (and two have four poster bed) and have the benefit of en suite bathrooms (with bath over shower, or separate shower), tea & coffee making facilities and flat screen TV. Four of the rooms are interconnecting via a lockable internal door enabling them to be sold as family rooms. Location: Situated to the northern side of the A551 Leasowe Road, the hotel is on the outskirts of the small residential settlements of Leasowe and Moreton, close to the northern extremity of the Wirral peninsula. Access to the national motorway network is gained at Junction 1 of the M53 motorway which is within 1½ miles to the east of the subject premises. The M53 connects with the M56 to the south of Ellesmere Port and, in turn, the M56 has direct access to the M6. The property benefits from mains sewage, water and electrics with the gas supply being recently converted to LPG. archive.address: Elen's Castle, Dolwyddelan, Conwy, LL25 0EJ
archive.description: Elen's Castle Hotel comprises an 18th century coaching inn of traditional construction, providing 14 bedrooms in total, along with a former coach house/stables. Internally, the ground floor contains the principal public areas comprising a breakfast and garden room/restaurant, for approximately 30 covers and a separate bar and lounge. The ground floor also provides a catering kitchen, preparation kitchen, walk‑in fridge, laundry room, office, storage area and an owners living room. The first floor comprises 8 en-suite units including, 6x double bedrooms, 3x bedroom family suite, 1x twin bedroom and a 3x bedroom owners room across the first and second floor. Along with an additional laundry room, storage and WC's. The coach houses/stables also provides an additional 1x bedroom bunk house and a secure indoor motorbike and bicycle storage area, extending to approximately 447 sq m (4,811 sq ft) GIA. Externally, the property benefits from grounds and gardens with an outside seating area for approximately 20 covers, a former Roman Well is also located on site providing spring water. There is also a large car parking area located opposite the hotel with x2 EV chargers, the total site area is approximately 0.608 hectares (1.502 acres). Location Elen’s Castle Hotel is prominently situated on the A470 in the village of Dolwyddelan, set within the Lledr Valley at the heart of Snowdonia National Park, providing convenient access to the surrounding countryside and key visitor destinations. Dolwyddelan lies between Betws‑y‑Coed and Blaenau Ffestiniog, with the wider Betws‑y‑Coed area attracting visitors year round due to its extensive range of walks and treks. Dolwyddelan Castle is located on the outskirts of the village and is only a short walk from the hotel. The property sits at the foot of Moel Siabod, in a position between Betws‑y‑Coed and the Crimea Pass, making it a well placed base for exploring the national park. The hotel is also ideally located for regional attractions, including Zip World, Ffestiniog Railway and Antur Stiniog Mountain Bike Centre. The Property, 47 St Giles Street is a principally two storey period Grade II Listed building with mezzanine, attic and extensive basement accommodation, forming part of the established historic townscape. The decorative Bath stone façade is executed in the neoclassical style with rusticated Tuscan columns and sash windows, giving the building strong architectural presence. Originally a 17th century house, the property was acquired by the Freemasons in 1879 and established as a Masonic Hall by 1881. The current structure was designed by Albert Havers and built in 1905–1906, with further remodelling in 1928. Until recently it operated as a Masonic club and events venue.. Freehold. Vacant. archive.description: Situation: The property is located in the heart of Gainsborough town centre, being a popular and traditional Lincolnshire market town. The town centre itself is undergoing significant regeneration thanks to Lottery Grant Funding. Many of the historic shop fronts have been, or are being restored, with the addition of residential conversions as well. There is also a Savoy Cinema complex recently completed and open, with additional retails/restaurant units. Nearby occupiers include Yorkshire Building Society, Boots, and a wide range of local and small business operators. Gainsborough itself is well positioned for access to the surrounding towns of Scunthorpe and Retford, along with Cities of Doncaster and Lincoln. archive.description: The property comprises part ground and extensive upper floor accommodation within the historic Royal Arcade, extending to approximately 2,189 sq m (23,562 sq ft) and benefitting from Planning Permission and Listed Building Consent for conversion and refurbishment to provide a 33-unit residential scheme together with six office suites. A residential scheme has been drawn up which illustrates the potential to create a substantial number of residential units above and/or behind the commercial accommodation, subject to the necessary consents. The property comprises the extensive upper floors of the historic Royal Arcade in the heart of Bournemouth town centre, presenting a rare opportunity to deliver a substantial residential-led refurbishment and conversion project with the planning position already established. The accommodation extends to approximately 2,183 sq m (23,500 sq ft) and benefits from Planning Permission and Listed Building Consent for the creation of a 33-unit residential scheme comprising a mix of one, two and three-bedroom apartments. Significantly, a substantial proportion of the accommodation already benefited from established residential use and consent, with further planning permissions subsequently secured for the additional units required to complete the approved scheme. The majority of the proposed apartments are already physically formed within the existing building configuration, having been historically occupied as residential accommodation. Numerous units retain substantial masonry divisions and existing layouts, with drainage infrastructure remaining at former residential locations, albeit purchasers should rely on their own investigations regarding condition and suitability. The approved scheme provides an attractive mix of accommodation, including numerous duplex apartments together with a number of generously proportioned two and three-bedroom units, several extending to in excess of 100 sq m. In addition, the property includes six office suites extending to approximately 306 sq m (3,294 sq ft), offering future asset management and potential development opportunities, subject to obtaining any necessary consents. Extensive sound testing has already been undertaken and a priced schedule of works has been prepared, providing purchasers with a significant body of due diligence information. Estimated Rental Values - Residential and office rental appraisal indicating an aggregate estimated rental value of approximately £495,660 per annum. Interested parties should rely on their own enquiries. Additional information Tenure Leasehold. Held for a term of 999 years from December 2012 at a peppercorn ground rent Accommodation Arranged over 23,562.3 sq ft (2,189 sq m ) Tenancy Vacant Planning The property benefits from Planning Permission (Ref 7-2024-16746-AZ) and Listed Building Consent (Ref 7-2019-16746-AS) for the refurbishment and conversion of the upper floors to provide a 33-unit residential scheme. A substantial number of the proposed apartments already benefited from residential consent and use, with the remaining units subsequently receiving planning consent to complete the approved 33-unit scheme. The planning position has therefore been comprehensively advanced, with significant work undertaken to secure the necessary consents and establish the residential redevelopment potential of the building. The approved accommodation comprises a mix of one, two and three-bedroom apartments, including a number of duplex units. In addition, the property incorporates six office suites which may offer future alternative use or redevelopment potential, subject to obtaining all necessary statutory consents. The approved 33-unit residential scheme comprises; 9 one-bedroom apartments averaging approximately 51 sq m 20 two-bedroom apartments averaging approximately 67 sq m 3 three-bedroom apartments averaging approximately 119 sq m 1 studio apartment of approximately 34 sq m Total residential accommodation extending to approximately 2,189 sq m (23,562 sq ft) Prospective purchasers should rely upon their own enquiries in respect of planning, listed building matters, Building Regulations, condition, services, drainage and all other technical matters prior to bidding. archive.address: 15 Heath Avenue, Littleover, Derby DE23 6DJ
archive.description: ** DEVELOPMENT & RENOVATION OPPORTUNITY WITH BUILDING PLOTS ** An attractive Edwardian detached property of style and character with double detached garage and this most generous mature garden plot. This substantial garden area includes a building plot with outline planning consent granted for the construction of two three bedroom semi-detached dwellings. The property is situated in this highly convenient cul-de-sac location in the heart of Littleover village close to an excellent range of local amenities and also located within the catchment area for Littleover School & Wren Park Primary School. A rare and exciting development opportunity to acquire an attractive, Edwardian three-bedroom detached residence, requiring modernisation, together with a valuable building plot benefiting from outline planning permission for the construction of two new semi-detached homes within the adjoining garden. The main property also has a gated driveway to the rear with access to a double detached garage. As part of the approved scheme, alterations will be required to the existing property to ensure that the principal windows of No. 15 Heath Avenue do not overlook the proposed new homes. Further details can be found on the local authority planning portal under application reference 24/01345/FUL The approved alterations to the existing house will create accommodation comprising an entrance hallway, guest cloakroom shower wc, an east-facing lounge, dining room, dining kitchen with a side porch/utility room. Upstairs, the first floor landing gives access to three bedrooms, master with en-suite shower room, two further bedrooms and a family bathroom. The proposed semi-detached properties will each comprise an entrance hallway, guest cloakroom wc, dining kitchen to the front elevation, and a rear lounge with bi-fold doors opening onto the garden. To the side will be a tandem driveway, while the first floor will provide three bedrooms and a family bathroom. Further details can be found on the local authority planning portal under application reference 24/01435/OUT We believe the proposed dwellings will prove highly desirable, occupying a popular and convenient residential position in the heart of Littleover village centre. The Location - The property occupies a convenient location just a short stroll from Littleover Village centre to include an excellent range of local shops and amenities. These include a supermarket, Post Office, petrol station, coffee shop and a further range of retail outlets. This location is also well positioned for employment opportunities at Rolls-Royce, Toyota, Derby University and The Royal Derby Hospital. There is also swift access to the A38 and A50 leading to the M1 motorway and the main motorway network The property also falls within the catchment area for the noted Littleover Community School and Wren Park Primary School. Private education is also within easy access at Derby High School and Derby Grammar School.

archive.address: Pack Horse Inn, Widdop Road, Widdop, Hebden Bridge, West Yorkshire HX7 7AT
archive.description: A rare opportunity to acquire a substantial freehold former country inn occupying an outstanding rural position within the Pennines, comprising a historic public house, extensive owner's accommodation, a separate four-bedroom house and a self-contained two-bedroom apartment. Dating back to 1610, the property sits within approximately 0.55 acres and enjoys panoramic views across open moorland, offering significant potential for a variety of redevelopment opportunities, such as a high-end residential scheme, subject to any necessary consents. The public house has traded successfully for centuries as a destination venue, particularly for food-led trade, benefiting from its position on the Pennine Way and close to Widdop Reservoir. Although the business ceased trading following the departure of the previous tenant in March 2025, the property retains a premises licence and presents an opportunity for a new operator to re-establish the business or explore alternative uses, subject to obtaining any required consents. The accommodation comprises a traditional bar arranged over two sections with catering kitchen and ancillary areas, together with generous three-bedroom owner's accommodation. Adjoining the pub is a deceptively spacious four-bedroom house with multiple reception rooms, whilst a separate self-contained two-bedroom apartment occupies the first and second floors above the integral garage/store. Externally, the property benefits from customer seating areas, gardens and a substantial car park serving the premises. Occupying an idyllic countryside setting approximately five miles from Hebden Bridge and eight miles from Colne, the property lies within an area renowned for walking, cycling and outdoor pursuits, attracting visitors throughout the year. Its unique character, sizeable accommodation and picturesque location combine to create an exceptional lifestyle and investment opportunity.

Post 47. Title number is ABN97934. Located on a low mound on the south side of a field boundary 150 yards east of an un-named minor road. Daily local bus service connecting with Aberdeen (26 miles). The Bunker was not required to fulfil its nuclear war role. With international relations having changed radically, the British government cancelled plans for upgrading and is sold on a freehold basis. Opened in 1962 and closed 1991. Secured with padlock entry. Freehold Sale. Full outright ownership. PRIME LOT IN EXCLUISVE AREA - VERY RARE TO MARKET - PRICED TO SELL. Alford is a large village in Aberdeenshire, north-east Scotland, lying just south of the River Don. It lies within the Howe of Alford which occupies the middle reaches of the River Don. United Kingdom Warning and Monitoring Organisation (UKWMO) Royal Observer Corps Post (ROC) Post. The bunker was designed to accommodate three people for two weeks. It has an underground monitoring room and a chemical toilet. All surface features remain intact with some flaking of the khaki paint. The unit is padlocked and secured. Title Number: ABN97934. Internally the post is very neat and tidy with many items remaining including WB1401 carrier receiver with WB1410 filter unit, Tele-talk, tool board, small wall mounted shelf, mirror, visitors log, various papers, ROC magazines, fire blanket in its box, dustpan, original canvas folding chair, FSM probe gasket, candle holder, light/wiring, BT junction boxes/wiring, BPI mount, posters, kettle, saucepan, washing bowl, cleaning materials, fuse box/wiring, net, pick axe, newspaper cutting about the post. On the wall the crew have written Stand Down - Best Post 29 Group. There is a wooden sign that says 47 Post Alford. Some items from the post have been donated to the Alford Heritage Centre where they have an ROC Room with artifacts from other local posts and Aberdeen Group HQ. Alford is a popular Donside Village which is well served by local shops, public transport facilities and excellent Primary and Secondary schools. The location offers easy access to Aberdeen City. The locality provides endless beautiful walks, stunning countryside, a variety of outdoor activities, and the Lecht Ski Centre and School is only a 30 minute drive away. Maps & Location Map Street View Satellite Alford is a swiftly growing rural town nestled in the splendour of the Aberdeenshire countryside, Alford is home to several visitor attractions including a museum, ski centre, golf course and woodland country park. For those adventure seekers, the town can also act as a base for walkers and cyclists hoping to explore Royal Deeside. Alford is a large village in Aberdeenshire, north-east Scotland, lying just south of the River Don. It lies within the Howe of Alford which occupies the middle reaches of the River Don. Located in the centre of the town is the renowned Grampian Transport Museum, boasting climb-aboard vintage vehicles, interactive exhibitions as well as special collections  enjoyed by adults and children alike. Close to some of Scotlands largest ski centres, the town is also great for perfecting your skill all-year round on the dry ski slope at the Alford Ski Centre. archive.address: The Croft, Hooke Hill, Freshwater, Isle Of Wight, PO40 9BG
archive.description: Bedrooms x 20 Bathrooms x 10 The Croft served the local community for many years as a residential care home registered for 22 live-in residents though the owners preferred to work with 20 occupied bedrooms for the sake of improved space and comfort requirements for their residents. The property was developed in three stages with the original house at the front of the site offering accommodation on two floors. Subsequently two extensions were added which significantly increase the footprint of the property as can be viewed in our aerial photography. The Croft has been closed as a care home for some years due to retirement with the current owner continuing to live in the owner's accommodation within the building. It is considered that the property offers scope and potential for a number of future uses, subject to all necessary consents being obtainable. Alternatively, site redevelopment may be a further option that prospective purchases may wish to consider, subject to all the necessary consents being obtainable. Accommodation 22 bedrooms, many with en-suite facilities, three communal lounges, kitchen, laundry room, dining room and office/conservatory, three further bath/shower rooms. Outside Substantial car parking area to the front and side, space for numerous vehicles in a courtyard garden side garden in need of cultivation. Auctioneer's Note In addition to the outside space detailed above, as can be viewed from the identification plan in the sales particulars, there is a long strip of land running to the southeast of The Croft. The current owner has had previously entered into negotiations with three neighbouring home owners with a view to transferring this land in sections to these home owners in return for a fee of £10,000 per parcel with the purchaser also meeting legal fees. This information is passed on as described to us by the current owner and prospective purchasers should of course rely on their own enquiries. Local Planning Authority Isle of Wight Council. Website: iow.gov.uk. Tel: 01983 823552. EPC Rating C (54). Total Floor Area 551 sq.m. Freehold with Vacant Possession The Croft, Hooke Hill, Freshwater, Isle Of Wight

archive.description: Freehold with vacant possession Central City location Additional area of land to side End of terrace single garage Description: A well-located end of terrace single garage in a popular residential area in the centre of Cambridge, close to allotments. The garage is of brick wall construction beneath a flat felt covered roof and has a concrete floor. There is a red metal up-and-over door to the front which is understood to have been re-strung and re-wired approximately 3 years ago. Inside, the garage has a maximum width of 2.61m and depth of 5.27m, with a height of 2.116m to the underside of the roof supports. The garage forms the end of a purpose-built block of garages with this being the furthest south east of the garages, at the end of the cul-de-sac. In addition to the garage there is an extra area of land lying to the left hand side (south) which is approximately 3.2m wide, on which there has previously been a storage shed. This area may provided added opportunities for storage/parking etc. The garage is clean and tidy and offers an ideal parking/storage opportunity for those looking for spaces in a central city location. The garage may also suit a user of the nearby allotments, as handy storage space. Tenure: Freehold with vacant possession

archive.description: Summary: Property Summary Freehold mixed use development opportunity Planning permission for 18x residential apartments, 6x commercial studios and 2x live/work units Proposed accommodation approximately 1,273 sq m (13,705 sq ft) Coastal location Site area approximately 0.09 hectares (0.23 acres) On the instructions of the Morgagee in Possession Vacant possession Particulars: The site extends to approximately 0.09 hectares (0.23 acres) and comprises a number of buildings with planning permission granted in three phases as follows: Phase 1 - conversion of the existing four storey building to provide 4x ground floor commercial studios and 12x residential apartments on the upper floors Phase 2 - conversion of the existing building to provide 2x ground floor commercial studios and 6x residential apartments on the upper floors Phase 3 - conversion of the existing Grade II Listed warehouse building into 2x live/work units comprising commercial ground floor studio accommodation and 2x two bedroom apartments above Some works for Phase 1 have been completed but prospective purchasers are to rely on their own enquiries in this regard. Location: Lowestoft lies on the east coast of England approximately 29 miles south east of Norwich and can be accessed via the A12, A47 and A146. The town is known for its long sandy beach, which stretched for several miles along the coast and is a draw for tourism into the town. Lowestoft railway station lies within a miles of the subject property and provides regional rail links and national rail services via nearby Norwich railway station. Additonally numerous bus routes serve the town and surrounding area and Norwich Airport lies approximately 34 miles to the north west. archive.description: A rare and unique opportunity to acquire a detached three-bedroom farmhouse located within a semi-rural position in North Burlingham. The property has been in the same ownership for many years and would now benefit from a programme of updating and offers the opportunity to extend subject to planning consent. The property has its own garden which is fenced with greenhouses, brick and timber stores. The remainder of the site offers three substantial steel framed agricultural buildings within a fenced parcel of land accessed by double metal gates. Previously used to store a variety agricultural machine these units could now offer a variety of uses subject to planning consent. Located approximately 2 miles east of Blofield where there is a host of village amenities and access on to the A47 trunk road giving good transport links to Norwich, Acle and Great Yarmouth where an abundance of high street shops, supermarkets, leisure activities including the Broads can be fund. Accommodation: Ground Floor: Entrance porch, entrance hall, lounge, dining room, kitchen, bathroom, rear hall stairs to first floor. First Floor: Landing, three bedrooms. archive.address: Wayside, Brookfield Drive, NOTTINGHAM, Nottinghamshire, NG14 7JW
archive.description: A four double bedroom, detached property located in the highly desirable village of Hoveringham. This is the first time that the property has been offered for sale, having been owned by the same family since it was built in the 1940s. The property requires a scheme of works throughout, presenting a huge opportunity to increase the value and make the property your own. The accommodation comprises an entrance hall, living room, dining room, two further reception rooms and a kitchen to the ground floor. There are five double bedrooms and a bathroom to the first floor. Externally, there are good sized gardens to the front and rear, with a driveway giving ample offroad parking. There is access to an outhouse, outside WC and coal store. There is also a garage and workshop, with both requiring attention and we haven’t been able to fully inspect the condition due to the overgrown garden. Hoveringham is a highly sought after village located approximately 12 miles from Nottingham city centre and approximately 15 miles from Newark. We’ve been informed that there isn’t a gas supply connected to the property. Offered for sale with the benefit of vacant possession. It is our understanding that the Property is not registered at the Land Registry which is the case with a significant proportion of land across England and Wales. Your conveyancer will take the necessary steps and advise you accordingly. archive.address: Corner House, 77 High Street,, Caythorpe, Grantham, NG32 3DP , & Corner House Cottage, 5 Church Lane,, GRANTHAM, Lincolnshire, NG32 3DU
archive.description: Offered for sale is a Grade II listed seven-bedroom property with an attached Grade II listed two-bedroom cottage annexe. There is flexible accommodation across the two properties, which are held on the same title register. There is pedestrian access over the courtyard with access to the properties from both road frontage and to the rear. The detached garage has been used as a home office and there is a staircase rising to the loft space. There is an inspection pit in the garage and double doors opening out onto Church Lane. Most recently, the properties have operated as a care home and there is scope to re-instate a care home, subject to necessary permissions and consents, whilst also providing the opportunity for other potential commercial uses. The property has been well maintained over the years and upgrades have been made sympathetically, in keeping with the character and history of the building. Caythorpe is a beautifully picturesque village in Lincolnshire, located approximately 9 miles from the market town of Grantham and 13 miles from Newark. There is a private and enclosed garden to the rear, including a lawned and patio area and a summer house. Offered for sale with the benefit of vacant possession. Accommodation for both properties Ground Floor: entrance hall, 7x reception rooms, kitchen, wet room, 4x WC. First Floor: 7x bedrooms, 2x WC ensuite, WC, bathroom, laundry room, laundry cupboard, utility room. External: detached garage. Pedestrian access over the courtyard area. Private garden. The properties have separate electric and water meters Electric heating, there is no gas in the village. archive.address: Frankwell, SHREWSBURY , Shropshire, SY3 8JY
archive.description: Location! Location! Location! Situated on the highly desirable central west side of Shrewsbury's historic town centre, this property is just a stone's throw from the town centre in Frankwell. Walk across the Welsh Bridge to Shrewsbury's vibrant town centre, offering an abundance of boutique shops and quirky independent stores tucked away in medieval alleyways. The town also boasts a fantastic array of cafes, restaurants, and wine bars, many of which sit right on the riverside. Don't forget the famous Quarry Park, which hosts superb events throughout the year. Within walking distance of some of Shrewsbury's most well-respected schools, sites, and attractions, living in Frankwell is a lifestyle choice. It sits in the heart of Shrewsbury, yet is just far enough away, surrounded by historic buildings that form the character and history we all love in Shrewsbury. Take a short walk and you can be sitting on the decking of The Boathouse next to the River Severn, enjoying a drink and some fantastic food. Being within walking distance of the train and bus stations is a real bonus; now add easy access to Shrewsbury's major roads heading west and south without even crossing the town centre. A little bit about the property This property is not just super-sized; it has so many options. Currently, the ground floor is used as a large retail shop with a separate stock room and a downstairs room that can be used as an office. The first floor is a very large two-bedroom apartment with a spacious kitchen-lounge-diner and a lovely bathroom, and bedroom two has its own WC. From the first floor, a separate stairwell leads to additional accommodation: a very useful studio apartment with its own en-suite shower room. It is worth noting that each floor has its own access. From an Investment Point of View This property has all the potential to generate a good return. We believe the shop portion could be rented out for around £2,000 per month, and the vendors already have an interested party. The first-floor apartment could also generate a minimum of £850 per month, and the studio apartment could generate £600 per month. That is a minimum expected yield of £3,450 per month, or £41,400 annually. There is also the potential to convert this property, with the correct planning consent, into three apartments or a single house. From a Homeowner's Point of View If you look at what this could become as a home, it is very exciting. With a total of 243 sq metres of living space, you could create—again, with the correct planning consent—something very special. Imagine a bright and airy open-plan ground floor utilising the front bay windows, an inner hallway with a large living room and kitchen-diner on either side, a separate utility room, and a playroom or study. The stairs to the first floor are wide and have lots of character. A rejig of the first floor could create three very large double bedrooms—and why not add an en-suite as well? This floor also has some great character features, including exposed wooden beams. Now, the second floor offers multi-generational living or the opportunity to generate extra income as a holiday let. That's food for thought! To top it off, the front of this property has real curb appeal, has lots of character, and complements the historic feel of Frankwell. Conclusion This is not just a property; it is an opportunity for investors or someone with vision who wants to create an iconic home in one of Shrewsbury's best locations. Converting this property into a house has the potential to add tremendous value, again with the correct planning consents. Council Tax Band: Band Not Applicable Tenure: Freehold

archive.address: Princes Avenue, Hull, East Riding of Yorkshire, HU5 3ES
archive.description: For sale via auction - fees, terms and conditions apply. This substantial property displays some the finest architectural features the Victorian period has to offer & in abundance! Occupying a prominent location on the sought after, Park Avenue & sat handsomely within a large front garden, behind wrought iron railings. The grand entrance archway, double vestibule doors & towering gables project one of the most notable facades on the Avenue. Stepping into the front porch you are greeted with the elegance & grandeur of the large entrance door, retaining the original stained glass with intricate patterns & craftmanship. Victorian wall tiling brings colour & period warmth to this porch, together making the greatest of first impressions to your visiting guests & a warming welcome home! As you enter the grand hallway you are met with pitch pine architrave, towering skirting & Lincrusta panelling. Large, ornate plasterwork adorns the ceiling, framed by a fabulous Lincrusta frieze & magnificent corbels support a vast central archway. The sitting room, presents 12" timber skirting, fabulous stepped plaster cornicing & an impressively detailed plasterwork rose to the ceiling. Natural daylight floods the room through a huge bay window, while your gaze is drawn to the elegant feature fire surround & cast iron fireplace within. The modern & calming colour palette makes this room bright & welcoming, the overwhelming feeling is of period grandeur in this room & throughout the rest of this property. Double, glazed doors lead through into the drawing room which is currently configured as a kitchen diner. You are again presented with an abundance of Victorian features on a grand scale including huge stepped cornicing, a grand ceiling rose, 12" timber skirting & a Victorian fitted cupboard with panelled doors. A further large walk-in bay window floods this beautiful reception room in natural daylight & offers views across the rear garden. The dining room is across the central hallway & up to the front of the property, this imposing & grand reception room boasts the West gables' huge bay window. Dramatic plaster cornicing adorns the ceiling, a magnificent plasterwork ceiling rose is the centre piece & focal point of this room while pitch pine sash windows, picture rails & gigantic skirting frame the room with period splendour. This room is currently configured as the principal suite of the hotel, with a large ensuite bathroom & vast proportions! Back out to the grand hallway & through to the rear of the property, you pass the craftmanship of the central staircase & a arrive at glazed door, leading out to the rear terrace patio & substantial grounds beyond. Off & to the left are the staff quarters, consisting of a rear lobby, a spacious staff or accessible W.C, the main kitchen, laundry corridor & laundry room. Beyond are the house managers accommodation, a spacious studio apartment with views across the rear garden. The wide, central, sweeping staircase is flanked by a decorative newel post, intricately carved from a solid piece of rich, polished Oak. The handrail of the same timber is atop a forest of carved spindles, leading up to a magnificent gallery landing. There is an exquisite 6-panel stained glass window on the mid landing which floods the whole area in vibrant colour with natural daylight, this Palatial reception hallway is drenched in period elegance. The vast central landing is a continuation of the grandeur of the reception hallway below, leading you to 6 generous bedrooms, four with ensuite bathrooms & a large office which sits above the front entrance door. Sweep around the galleried balustrade & through a further archway & you arrive at an internal lobby, a flight of stairs leads up to the 2nd floor accommodation & doors lead to a guest W.C & a further landing beyond which provides access to two further shower rooms & another guest W.C. Up to the second floor & you arrive at the bedroom corridor where you presented with a further five, spacious, double bedrooms, all with ensuite bathrooms. Out & to the rear of the property is bright & spacious courtyard garden, sandstone steps lead down from the house to a terraced patio of crazy paving & from here is a lawned area, finishing at a raised border with mature planting. The grounds open up to further more substantial lawn which encircle a magnificent weeping Willow beyond which is the secure walled car park. archive.description: 29 29 Bowlish, Bowlish, Shepton Mallet, Somerset, BA4 5JB Guide Price £750,000 Business rates & charges may apply View brochure SIZE Ask agent SECTOR Hotel for sale Key features Imposing Grade II* listed Palladian house dating from 1732 Established eight-bedroom hotel and hospitality venue Impressive reception rooms, ballroom and garden-facing orangery Suitable for boutique accommodation, weddings, events and exclusive hire Rich architectural, hospitality and local historical significance Extensive hotel fixtures, fittings and contents understood to be included, subject to inventory Potential for alternative or residential use, subject to all necessary consents Description For sale via auction - fees, terms and conditions apply. Dating from 1732, Bowlish House is an imposing Grade II* listed Palladian property offering an exceptional combination of architectural significance, established hospitality use and exciting future potential. Situated within the historic hamlet of Bowlish on the western edge of Shepton Mallet, this substantial eight-bedroom hotel has welcomed residents, travellers, diners, wedding parties and private guests for generations. Behind its elegant and beautifully balanced façade lies a wonderfully characterful collection of bedrooms, reception rooms, dining and entertaining spaces. Bowlish House is far more than a conventional hotel. It is a property shaped by nearly three centuries of history, adaptation and reinvention — a private house that evolved into a country hotel, a respected restaurant with rooms, a wedding and celebration venue, an exclusive-use retreat and an atmospheric location for photography and filming. Now offered for sale by auction, it represents a rare opportunity for a new owner to continue that story. The Property The approach to Bowlish House immediately establishes its presence. Its classical Palladian frontage, traditional sash windows, stone detailing and architectural symmetry create a striking first impression, while original and historic features found throughout the building reinforce its Grade II* status. The main house provides eight individually styled guest bedrooms together with an impressive range of communal accommodation. The reception spaces are one of the property’s greatest strengths. Generously proportioned lounges and dining rooms provide welcoming areas for hotel guests, private dining, afternoon teas and intimate celebrations. The ballroom creates a memorable setting for weddings, events, music, dining and larger gatherings, while the orangery provides a light-filled connection between the house and gardens. Throughout the property, period character is combined with the practical accommodation required for hospitality use. Decorative panelling, the traditional staircase, fireplaces, high ceilings and individual room layouts give Bowlish House an identity that would be difficult to reproduce within a modern hotel building. Eight Guest Bedrooms The hotel accommodation comprises eight individually presented bedrooms, offering guests a distinctive alternative to standardised chain-hotel accommodation. The rooms vary in size, design and character, making them suitable for leisure stays, wedding guests, exclusive-use bookings and private group accommodation. Their individuality forms an important part of the Bowlish House experience and provides an excellent foundation for a boutique hospitality operator wishing to develop a strong and memorable brand. Prospective purchasers should to the floorplans and legal documentation for the precise room arrangement, bathroom provision and accommodation schedule. Weddings, Events and Exclusive Use Bowlish House offers considerable potential as an intimate wedding and events destination. Its combination of reception rooms, ballroom, orangery, guest bedrooms and garden areas allows celebrations to take place under one roof, with accommodation available for principal guests. The house is particularly well suited to buyers seeking an alternative to larger and more corporate wedding venues. Alongside weddings, the property could accommodate private dining, milestone celebrations, corporate retreats, creative workshops, Christmas and New Year gatherings, wellness stays and exclusive-use weekends. The opportunity is not simply to sell rooms, but to sell the experience of having an historic Somerset house available for a private occasion. Hotel and Hospitality Opportunity Bowlish House has an established history as a hotel and restaurant with rooms. For an experienced hotelier, chef, events operator or hospitality entrepreneur, the property provides the chance to relaunch and reposition an existing destination without having to create the character of the building from the ground up. Its future could include a boutique hotel, restaurant with rooms, wedding venue, exclusive-use retreat, private members’ destination or a combination of complementary uses. archive.address: Barby Lane, Barby, Rugby, Warwickshire, CV23 8UX
archive.description: For Sale Via Online Auction. Fees Apply. We are delighted to offer for sale this attractive parcel of pasture land extending to approximately 5.23 acres, occupying a highly accessible position on the southern outskirts of Rugby with direct road frontage onto Barby Lane. This versatile parcel of land offers an excellent opportunity for those seeking agricultural or equestrian use, benefiting from a level layout and being divided into three well-fenced paddocks, enclosed by mature hedgerows and established trees which provide both privacy and shelter. The land enjoys direct vehicular access from Barby Lane via a secure steel-gated entrance. Positioned adjacent to the entrance is a useful timber-framed agricultural building with breeze block construction, tiled flooring and a clear PVC sheet roof, together with a small extension. Towards the rear of the land is a further timber pole lean-to, providing additional storage or shelter. Extending to approximately 5.23 acres, the land is classified as Grade 3 agricultural land and consists predominantly of base-rich loam and clay soils. The pasture is relatively level and still displays areas of historic ridge and furrow, adding to its rural character. A natural watercourse runs through the land, providing a convenient natural water supply and drinking point for livestock, making the holding particularly well suited for grazing. Ideally situated between the popular suburb of Hillmorton and the sought-after village of Barby, the land enjoys a peaceful rural setting whilst remaining conveniently located approximately three miles from Rugby town centre and around four miles from Junction 18 of the M1 motorway, offering excellent links to the M1, M6, A5 and A14. The property is offered for sale freehold with vacant possession. Prospective purchasers should note that the sale will be subject to a 30-year overage clause, reserving 30% of any uplift in value resulting from future non-agricultural or non-equestrian development. The overage will be triggered upon either the implementation of planning permission or any future sale. The property is also subject to a restrictive covenant preventing the erection or placement of any dwelling, caravan, house on wheels, temporary building or encampment intended for residential occupation. A public footpath crosses the centre of the land, and purchasers should satisfy themselves as to its position. The land is enclosed by fencing, and whilst every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy of the plan and description, these are provided for identification purposes only. Description An attractive parcel of pasture land extending to approximately 5.23 acres, occupying a highly accessible position on the southern outskirts of Rugby with direct road frontage onto Barby Lane. archive.description: Online auction 12th-13th October 2026 Grade 2* Listed Hotel with 48 Ensuite Letting Rooms This Grade 2* listed hotel offers 48 en-suite letting rooms along with 4 large function rooms and 30 additional restaurant dining areas. Externally there is also onsite parking for approx. 70 vehicles. The total site area covers approx. 2.24 hectares / 5.53 acres with the internal floor area totalling approx. 4,598.3 m2 / 49,496 sqft. The accommodation of the property comprises of: Conference and Function Accommodation: The hotel has significant conference/banqueting capability with the largest room being the Castle Suite, to the rear and on the ground floor, capable of seating up to 250 diners (circa 300 theatre style) but also able to divide into two smaller rooms of approximately half the size each. This room has the benefit of its own bar servery area and is located immediately adjacent to the main hotel kitchens. There is also a raised stage/performance area to the extreme west side of the room. To the rear this has been converted to a further function room known as ‘The Keep’ and is used for civil ceremonies, capable of seating circa 100+ people. At first floor level is a private meeting/function/dining room capable of seating circa 38 people. Both these elements can be separately accessed directly from the car park area. To the first floor is a further function room known as the Turret Suite, which comprises two interconnecting rooms to the eastern side of the hotel, partially within the 1987 addition and above the Wreckers Bar and coffee shop. These rooms have a seated capacity of circa 100. Reception Area / Lounges: The main reception office/desk and reception hall are located at ground floor level of the original towers on the east facing elevation and accessed directly from the car park. The entrance hall benefits from an attractive feature staircase leading to the letting bedrooms within the upper floors of the turrets. To the immediate right of the ground floor reception hall is the Star Chamber Lounge which has been furnished with various chairs, settees and coffee tables. There is also a 4-passenger lift (300kg) giving access between the ground floor and third floor. Food and Beverage (F&B) Areas: The Wreckers Bar and adjoining coffee shop are situated at ground floor level within the 1987addition. The Wreckers Bar has a seated capacity of circa 30 and has its own separate access as well as the benefit of access to the enclosed side external lawned area which doubles as a beer garden. The Coffee shop has a seated capacity of circa 16 and is situated between the Wreckers Bar and the main reception hall (and can accessed from either). Each contain a bar servery. In addition, accessed via a corridor from the main reception hall, is the Brasserie 1593 restaurant area, which has a dining capacity of circa 30 and which also has its own bar servery area. Letting Bedrooms: The hotel provides a total of 48 letting bedrooms situated at first, second and third floor levels throughout the property. A total of 8 rooms are situated within the original castellated section (2 at first floor level and 6 and second floor level including two suites/four poster bedrooms) and the remaining 40 rooms are provided towards the rear, within the 1900’s section (15 at first, 16 at second and 9 at third floor levels). All rooms are either provided with double or twin beds (and two have four poster bed) and have the benefit of en suite bathrooms (with bath over shower, or separate shower), tea & coffee making facilities and flat screen TV. Four of the rooms are interconnecting via a lockable internal door enabling them to be sold as family rooms. Location: Situated to the northern side of the A551 Leasowe Road, the hotel is on the outskirts of the small residential settlements of Leasowe and Moreton, close to the northern extremity of the Wirral peninsula. Access to the national motorway network is gained at Junction 1 of the M53 motorway which is within 1½ miles to the east of the subject premises. The M53 connects with the M56 to the south of Ellesmere Port and, in turn, the M56 has direct access to the M6. The property benefits from mains sewage, water and electrics with the gas supply being recently converted to LPG.
